rv.q: Fleetwood-Jourdain Theatre’s meditative revival, directed by Tim Rhoze, thoughtfully brings out the play’s themes of family and community.
The dynamics within the cast shine, bringing to life the theme of family and community.
But the beauty of the set and the dazzling dialogue become monotonous without conflicts that drive character development.
A poignant and award-winning script by Elyzabeth Gregory Wilder is at the core of this tightly woven narrative which spans the years 1939 to 2002.
Wilder's play is a well-written work with interesting characters and poignant messages. Plan a trip to Fleetwood-Jourdain Theatre to see this gem.

cn.t: Critics praise "Gee's Bend" for its poignant storytelling and emotional power, celebrating how it honors the multigenerational quilting tradition of Alabama's Black women through Elyzabeth Gregory Wilder's award-winning script and stunning production.
